notes.label: Build a new three-stage boundary-release room with a recoverable access guard, a lateral latch and a vertical exit bolt.
notes.goal: Build a new three-stage boundary-release room with a recoverable access guard, a lateral latch and a vertical exit bolt.
notes.change: Use a vertical preparation guard to occupy both possible right-push faces of an L latch. Its downward parking should expose the latch input; lateral latch displacement should detach a roof-blocked contact cluster; lifting the bolt should open the gem passage.
notes.reason: This introduces a reusable floor parking bay and a face-access dependency rather than reproducing the official disposal sequence or its staircase silhouettes. Every stage will be checked against complete-goal bypasses and first-opportunity exclusions.
expectedChecks: same roof removal enables blocked cluster push and bypasses latch-right

notes.label: Repair the unsolved layout while retaining the guard-parking, release and bolt-lift dependency.
notes.goal: Repair the unsolved layout while retaining the guard-parking, release and bolt-lift dependency.
notes.change: Move the latch's lower prong to its upper-right corner and supply its eastward swept clearance. Move the matched roof stops to (7,4) and (8,3).
notes.reason: The official solver exhausted 1,052 action states without a solution. Ordinary probing shows that the lower prong recruits the bolt during each rightward latch push, carrying it into the eastern dead end instead of detaching it. The upper prong avoids that unwanted lateral contact while retaining roof restriction and a blocked leftward shift.
expectedChecks: rightward latch displacement is independent of the bolt

notes.label: Eliminate the complete-goal bypass that avoids lifting the passage bolt.
notes.goal: Eliminate the complete-goal bypass that avoids lifting the passage bolt.
notes.change: Close the two unused northeast cells (9,6) and (10,6), which are no longer needed after relocating the latch prong.
notes.reason: Official search found and ordinary replay confirmed a 17-input completion with a downward bolt push. The newly free top of the bolt allowed the player to bypass via the open northeast shoulder. Closing those unused cells makes the intended y=7 passage the only connection to the gem branch.
expectedChecks: bolt-up before the complete gem goal
ordinary replay of the complete revised route

notes.label: Finalize the locally verified three-stage room and preserve replayable evidence.
notes.goal: Finalize the locally verified three-stage room and preserve replayable evidence.
notes.change: Retain the third geometric layout and bind the legal 21-input route to stage inputs 9, 11 and 17. Build it with the installed complex builder and collect complete ordinary-engine replay frames from the saved build.
notes.reason: The formal complex verifier reports passed on all 20 checks, including first-opportunity dependencies, necessary-role exclusions and the matched roof intervention. A legal witness uses two downward guard pushes, two eastward latch pushes and one upward bolt push. This is author-side structural evidence, not an independent model evaluation or measured human difficulty.
expectedChecks: saved build cells equal verified design
ordinary and search transitions agree at every input

notes.label: Verify browser Undo and Reset under the supported pre-collection conditions.
notes.goal: Verify browser Undo and Reset under the supported pre-collection conditions.
notes.change: Run Undo/Reset in a fresh browser storage context after the first push, before collecting the gem.
notes.reason: The first browser test matched all 21 ordinary play states, then failed because it expected a collected gem to reappear after Undo. The existing browser checker explicitly uses a fresh storage context to avoid gem persistence. This is a correction to the test setup, not a map change.

First-push Undo and Reset match saved pre-collection states
